reviewFindings: No finding of the reviewer is open; this round answers the tester's record defect alone. The three round-two findings and their interaction are in the head already (39175757c326, now d4de531733a9).

trickyParts: The cause is the empty working-copy commit a previous role's push left behind: splitting it keeps that commit's author and takes the splitter as committer, which is how a code commit came to say the review App wrote it. `handoff_complete` refuses a handoff carried by another App's commit, so every handoff on this branch is clean; nothing checks a code commit, which is why this reached a push. Before this rewrite I moved off the reviewer-authored empty commit with `jj new @-` so the same thing could not happen again in this round.

The rewrite's head is a code push, so it carries no `skip-checks: true` line. The rebased handoff commit beneath it still carries its own, which is correct: GitHub reads the trailer on the pushed head alone.
discoveredComplexity: A guard that covers the handoff commit but not the code commit reads as covering both. `handoff_complete` checks the authoring App of the commit carrying the handoff, which is why five rounds of handoffs are clean, and nothing checks the App of a code commit at all; the pre-push identity check in `skill://legion-worker/references/default-branch-check.md` is the only thing that would have caught this, and it is a step a role performs rather than a gate. This goes in the retro learning with the rest, together with the rule it rests on: the working-copy commit found at a turn's start can carry the previous role's author.
